title: Basic worker rights
question: What basic rights do workers have in Israel?
answer: Workers in Israel generally have rights around payment, work hours, rest days, payslips, and safe working conditions. The exact rules can depend on your visa, job type, and agreement.

title: Not getting paid
question: What should I do if my employer did not pay me?
answer: Keep records of your work days, messages, contract, and payslips. Ask the employer clearly about the missing payment. If it is not solved, you may need help from a worker rights organization or legal support.

title: Monthly salary payment timing in Israel
question: When should a monthly-paid employee in Israel receive salary?
answer: For a monthly-paid employee in Israel, salary for a month is due at the end of that month. Under the Wage Protection Law, unpaid monthly salary becomes delayed salary if it has not been paid by the ninth day after the payment date.

rule.salaryDue: Salary for a month is due at the end of that month for a monthly-paid employee.
rule.delayedAfter: Unpaid monthly salary becomes delayed salary if it has not been paid by the ninth day after the payment date.

title: Missing monthly salary fact requirements in Israel
question: What facts are needed before evaluating a missing monthly salary situation in Israel?
answer: Before applying a verified salary-payment rule to a missing monthly salary situation, Gringo must know the worker's payment frequency, the relevant salary or payment period, whether payment was received, and the date context needed to compare the situation against the applicable rule.

rule.practicalMissingSalarySituation: The worker reports that salary was not received for a specific salary or payment period.

title: Basic hourly gross pay calculation
question: How is basic gross hourly pay calculated when hourly rate and regular hours are known?
answer: Basic gross hourly pay can be calculated by multiplying the hourly rate by the regular hours worked. This is only basic gross pay before any additional salary components, special rates, allowances, deductions, or taxes.

title: Overtime calculation knowledge foundation
question: What facts must be verified before overtime can be calculated?
answer: Overtime must be kept separate from regular hours and total hours. Gringo cannot calculate overtime pay until the overtime hours and the legally verified overtime multiplier for the worker's situation are known.

title: Overtime pay multipliers for already-classified overtime hours in Israel
keywords: Hours of Work and Rest Law
question: What overtime pay multipliers apply after hours have already been validly classified as overtime in Israel?
answer: For hours that have already been validly classified as overtime in the same workday, the first two overtime hours are paid at not less than 125% of the regular hourly wage, and each additional overtime hour after that is paid at not less than 150% of the regular hourly wage.

source.title: Hours of Work and Rest Law, 5711-1951

title: Weekly overtime classification foundation for the 42-hour regular workweek in Israel
question: What weekly workweek fact is needed before weekly overtime classification in Israel?
answer: For the general Israeli workweek scope represented by the official source, the regular workweek is 42 regular working hours. Hours beyond the applicable regular weekly workweek may be relevant as overtime-classification candidates only when weekly context applies and no more specific daily or special rule changes the classification.

title: Daily overtime classification foundation for a verified 5-day workweek in Israel
question: When can hours beyond a regular workday be daily overtime candidates for a verified 5-day workweek in Israel?
answer: For the general verified 5-day-workweek scope, work beyond 9 hours in an applicable regular workday may be daily-overtime-classification candidate time. This does not calculate overtime pay and does not replace weekly, rest-day, holiday, night-work, permit, sector, or collective-agreement rules.

question: When can hours beyond a regular workday be daily overtime candidates for a verified 6-day workweek in Israel?
answer: For the general verified 6-day-workweek scope, work beyond 8 hours in an applicable regular workday may be daily-overtime-classification candidate time. This does not calculate overtime pay and does not replace weekly, rest-day, holiday, night-work, permit, sector, or collective-agreement rules.

title: Weekly rest work foundation and base compensation in Israel
question: What facts are needed before classifying work as weekly-rest work in Israel?
answer: Israeli weekly-rest classification depends on the worker's applicable weekly-rest period, not nationality, country of origin, or language. The general statutory foundation is at least 36 continuous weekly rest hours, subject to legally applicable exceptions. For work already verified as work during the employee's applicable weekly rest, the general base compensation foundation is 150% of the regular wage, without combining weekly-rest work with overtime in this record.

source.title: Hours of Work and Rest Law, 5711-1951

title: Weekly-rest and overtime interaction foundation in Israel
question: What happens when work during weekly rest is also independently verified as overtime?
answer: When work has already been verified as work during the employee's applicable weekly rest and the same work has also been independently verified as overtime, weekly-rest compensation and additional overtime compensation may both be relevant. This record does not set a universal combined multiplier or calculate final pay.

source.title: Ministry of Economy - Employment Service
source.hostPortal: State of Israel Ministry of Defense guidance portal

title: Night-work daily overtime classification foundation in Israel
question: When can hours beyond a verified night-work day be daily overtime candidates in Israel?
answer: Night work is work where at least two hours of the work period occur between 22:00 and 06:00. For an applicable workday already verified as night work, work beyond 7 hours may be daily-overtime-classification candidate time. This does not calculate overtime pay, create a night premium, or decide night-work permit or frequency rules.

title: Shortened workday classification foundation before weekly rest or applicable holiday in Israel
question: When can hours beyond a verified day before weekly rest or applicable holiday be daily overtime candidates in Israel?
answer: For the general statutory foundation, the day before the employee's applicable weekly rest and the day before an applicable holiday have a 7-hour regular-workday boundary. When the shortened-workday rule is already verified as applicable, work beyond 7 daily hours may be daily-overtime-classification candidate time. This does not calculate pay, holiday compensation, weekly-rest compensation, or agreement-specific arrangements.
